name: Pseudoxanthomatous Diffuse Cutaneous Mastocytosis
aliases: Diffuse Cutaneous Mastocytosis with Pseudoxanthomatous Lesions

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse, yellowish to orange pseudoxanthomatous cutaneous lesions
Histopathological confirmation of dense mast cell infiltration in the dermis
Positive Darier's sign (urtication and erythema upon stroking lesions)
Elevated serum tryptase levels above age-adjusted normal range
No evidence of systemic mastocytosis on bone marrow or organ biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (diffuse pseudoxanthomatous lesions and dermal mast cell infiltration) with supportive clinical signs such as positive Darier's sign or elevated serum tryptase
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and histopathological; systemic involvement must be excluded.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic diffuse skin involvement with thickened, yellowish plaques
Urtication and erythema upon stroking lesions
searchTerms: redness and swelling on skin irritation

common.notes: Itching often exacerbated by heat or friction
Transient erythema and warmth due to mast cell mediator release

common.symptomName: Blistering of affected skin in infancy
common.notes: Tense bullae may develop on involved areas

occasional.notes: Due to mast cell mediator effects on GI tract
searchTerms: intestinal cramps and frequent bowel movements

occasional.symptomName: Headache associated with mast cell activation
searchTerms: headache linked to mast cell activation
head pain with mast cell symptoms

occasional.notes: Occasional involvement of oral or pharyngeal mucosa

rare.notes: Severe systemic mast cell mediator release
Due to systemic mast cell mediator effects

laboratory: Normal complete blood count except possible mild eosinophilia
imaging: Usually normal; bone imaging if musculoskeletal symptoms present
other: Histopathology showing dense dermal mast cell infiltration with spindle-shaped mast cells
Positive Darier's sign on physical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic organ involvement including bone marrow
Presence of systemic symptoms such as hepatosplenomegaly
Histiocytic rather than mast cell infiltration
Solitary or few nodules rather than diffuse plaques

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with blistering
references: Castells M. Mastocytosis: classification, diagnosis, and management. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2018;32(1):153-169.
Valent P, Akin C, Metcalfe DD. Mastocytosis: 2016 updated WHO classification and novel emerging treatment concepts. Blood. 2017;129(11):1420-1427.
